extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and experts asked to review NSF grant proposals (NSF peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting merit reviews of NSF proposals, including pre-review preparation, how to apply merit review criteria, writing constructive reviews, and avoiding bias. Targeted at individuals serving as NSF proposal reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch reviewer orientation video before reading proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have been asked to review one or more proposals for the U.S. National Science Foundation, please watch the reviewer orientation video below before you begin to read the proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View the recommended 'The Art and Science of Reviewing Proposals' video to orient to NSF expectations before starting any proposal review; afterwards, provide feedback via the Merit Review Video Feedback survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read and decide how to apply the merit review criteria before reading proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the merit review criteria before you read the proposal(s). Decide how you will apply the criteria and stick to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish application of the criteria up front and maintain that approach for each proposal to ensure consistent evaluation. Avoid introducing new criteria while reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not shift or vary criteria between proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not shift your criteria as you go from evaluating one proposal to the next, and do not include extraneous data or criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same standards across proposals and avoid adding irrelevant factors or extra data that are not part of the stated review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take notes when reading the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Take notes when reading the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record observations, strengths, weaknesses, and supporting examples while reading to support later judgments and writing of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include a lengthy summary of the proposal in your review
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include a lengthy summary of the proposal in your review!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the review on evaluation relative to criteria rather than reproducing proposal content; brief context is acceptable but avoid long restatements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be constructive in your feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Be constructive in your feedback; is this the type of review you would like to receive?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actionable, professional comments that help applicants understand weaknesses and how to improve; avoid dismissive or non-specific criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: List strengths and weaknesses with respect to the review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: List strengths and weaknesses with respect to the review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments around the official merit review criteria, explicitly noting what aspects of the proposal meet or fail to meet each criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: In the summary state whether the proposal is competitive and why
rubrics_metrics.description: In the summary section of your review, tell us whether or not you believe the proposal is competitive and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concisely state a recommendation about competitiveness and justify it with reference to key strengths and weaknesses tied to the criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include concrete examples from the proposal to support points
rubrics_metrics.description: Include concrete examples from the proposal in support of the points in your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific sections, data, or statements from the proposal that illustrate the strengths or weaknesses you identify to make evaluations verifiable and precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and mitigate cognitive biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for signs of the impact of cognitive biases in what you write and strive to mitigate these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of potential biases (e.g., confirmation bias, halo/horn effects, affinity bias) and actively check whether judgments are supported by facts rather than impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency and objectivity across multiple reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are reviewing multiple proposals, are your reviews consistent and objective?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare standards and language used across reviews to avoid leniency/harshness drift; apply the same interpretation of criteria to all proposals you review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternative views and whether they are justified by facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Think of alternative views and consider whether they are justified based on facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately seek plausible counter-arguments to your assessment and evaluate whether evidence in the proposal supports or refutes those alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play devil's advocate to your own assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Play a devil's advocate to your own assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge your initial conclusions to test their robustness and reduce unexamined assumptions in your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review your notes before finalizing the review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisit your reading notes to ensure the review accurately reflects the evidence and that no important points were missed or misremembered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take time, pause, and reflect on your recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Take time, pause and reflect on your recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rushing to a final score; give yourself time to reflect and ensure the recommendation is deliberative and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critically read each review after writing; ensure judgments are justified in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Critically read each review after you have written it; ask yourself whether each judgment is clearly justified in the text of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit for clarity and evidence: every evaluative statement should point to supporting rationale or proposal content so program officers and applicants can follow your reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be accountable and imagine justifying your decision to others
rubrics_metrics.description: Be accountable to yourself and imagine justifying your decision to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write reviews as if you might have to explain and defend your recommendation publicly or to colleagues; this encourages clarity, fairness, and thorough justification.
